Options_Considered: (A) Equal weights; (B) Expert-judged weights; (C) Data-driven weights (PCA/regression); (D) Literature-derived weights
Decision: [TO BE DECIDED AND APPROVED] Indicative baseline: Flow_Accumulation=30%; Slope=20%; River_Distance=20%; Rainfall=20%; Land_Cover=10%
Rationale: Flow accumulation is the primary terrain driver of flood concentration. Slope and river proximity capture flood susceptibility. Rainfall is the primary climatic driver. Land cover modifies runoff. These indicative weights reflect standard flood hazard index literature for West Africa. MUST be approved by PI before computation. Weights CANNOT be changed after seeing output.
Sensitivity_Model: Equal weights (20% each for all 5 inputs) as sensitivity model S1
Notes: CRITICAL: Weights must be pre-specified and locked. Running the model and then adjusting weights to match expected patterns is not acceptable. Sensitivity model S1 (equal weights) must also be computed and results compared. The baseline model is used for all primary outputs.

Options_Considered: (A) Equal-interval (0-20/20-40/40-60/60-80/80-100); (B) Quantile breaks; (C) Natural breaks (Jenks); (D) Expert-defined thresholds
Decision: [TO BE DECIDED] Recommended: Natural breaks (Jenks) on the study area distribution — produces most defensible classification given non-uniform index distribution. Alternative: Equal interval if comparability across states is required.
Rationale: Natural breaks classification minimises within-class variance and captures natural discontinuities in the hazard index distribution. However it makes cross-study comparison harder. Equal interval is simpler but may over-classify low-variation areas. Decision must be made before classification is run.
Sensitivity_Model: Run same output with equal-interval classification as sensitivity check
Notes: Classes: Very Low / Low / Moderate / High / Very High. These five classes are fixed — do not add or remove classes. Exact threshold values determined by chosen method applied to study area distribution.

Parameter: Spatial analysis method and minimum sample density
Options_Considered: (A) Point mapping only (<10 sites); (B) Simple KDE (10-19 sites); (C) Severity-weighted KDE (>=20 sites); (D) Spatial statistics/clustering (>=30 sites)
Decision: Tiered approach based on sample density — method determined per state/analysis zone after G26 is CLEAN. Severity-weighted KDE recommended where density permits. Point mapping only where density insufficient. No method selected globally until sample density assessed.
Rationale: No spatial statistical method may be applied merely because it is available. Sample density must be verified per analysis zone before method selection. The specification explicitly requires this.
Sensitivity_Model: Simple (unweighted) KDE as sensitivity check where severity-weighted KDE used
Notes: Bandwidth for KDE: 5km default search radius (based on typical community catchment size in Nigeria). Sensitivity test with 3km and 10km bandwidths recommended. Document bandwidth and rationale in processing notes.

Parameter: Validation acceptance threshold for G25 observed events
Options_Considered: Options: 60% / 70% / 80% / 90% of High-confidence G25 events falling in Moderate+ hazard zones
Decision: 70% of High-confidence G25 events must fall in Moderate/High/Very High hazard zones
Rationale: 70% represents a defensible validation threshold for a data-limited multi-criteria index model. It acknowledges that not all observed flood events are in locations that would score highest on terrain/rainfall metrics alone (e.g. flash floods in atypical locations). Below 70% triggers model review.
Notes: If validation score < 70%: review input weights (HMD01); check G25 data quality; consider adding additional inputs. Do NOT lower the threshold to achieve a pass.

Options_Considered: (A) Min-max to 0-100; (B) Z-score then rescale; (C) Percentile rank
Decision: Min-max normalisation to 0-100 for all inputs. Reference bounds fixed at study area extent at baseline — do not recalculate bounds at each update.
Rationale: Min-max is standard for multi-criteria index models. Reference bounds must be fixed at baseline to ensure consistency across update cycles. Recalculating bounds at each update would change all existing scores when new data is added — violating updateability principle.
Notes: River_Distance input: invert before normalisation (smaller distance = higher hazard). Flow_Accumulation: log-transform before normalisation (skewed distribution). Document all transformations in processing script.

Decision: Max-distance minus distance (linear inversion): Hazard_from_distance = (max_dist - dist) / max_dist * 100. Max distance capped at BUF001 value (500m) — beyond 500m hazard contribution from proximity = 0.
Rationale: Linear inversion is simple and reproducible. Capping at BUF001 (500m) is consistent with the documented buffer rationale. Exponential decay would require an additional parameter — avoid unless justified.
Notes: Max distance for normalisation = BUF001 = 500m. Cells beyond 500m from any river receive proximity score = 0 for this component only — other components still contribute to overall hazard score.

Options_Considered: (A) Equal weights NDVI+RUSLE+LC; (B) NDVI-dominant; (C) RUSLE-dominant; (D) Approved weights as specified
Decision: [TO BE DECIDED] Indicative baseline: NDVI trend 40% + RUSLE 40% + LC change 20%
Rationale: NDVI trend and RUSLE soil loss are the two most direct measures of land degradation; equal weight between them is defensible. Land cover change (20%) is a leading indicator of future degradation risk. This weighting must be approved before G50 computation.
Notes: Cannot compute LD_Score until HMD07 is recorded. LC change component requires two WorldCover epochs — use NDVI trend as proxy at baseline if only one epoch available; document this substitution.

Parameter: Forest canopy threshold definition and DF_Score weights
Decision: 30% canopy cover threshold (consistent with Hansen GFC standard methodology). DF_Score weights: deforestation rate 35% + forest proximity 35% + patch size 30%.
Rationale: 30% is the internationally standard threshold in Hansen GFC and is used by Global Forest Watch. FAO 10% would include much more area as forest and may overestimate coverage in already degraded landscapes. Consistency with Hansen GFC reporting is essential for auditability.
Sensitivity_Model: Run with 10% threshold as sensitivity check; report difference in community classification
Notes: Forest threshold MUST be identical between G51 (baseline) and G52 (current) — mixing thresholds invalidates G53 change detection.

Options_Considered: (A) Habitat integrity dominant; (B) Deforestation dominant; (C) Equal weights; (D) Approved weights
Decision: [TO BE DECIDED] Indicative: Habitat integrity deficit 35% + Deforestation rate 30% + PA gap 20% + Riparian deficit 15%
Rationale: Habitat integrity captures the current state most directly. Deforestation rate captures the primary driver of ongoing loss. PA gap captures the institutional protection response. Riparian condition captures a particularly sensitive and ecologically valuable habitat type.
Sensitivity_Model: Equal weights (25% each) as sensitivity S1
Notes: IND17 (deforestation) is reused from G54 in G63 — this is appropriate as deforestation is both a land degradation AND biodiversity pressure. Not double-counting because LD and BL are separate risk components in ERI v2.0.

Decision: [APPROVED: Baseline per ENVIRONMENTAL_DOMAINS_EXTENSION.md Section 6] H=0.25; E=0.15; V=0.15; C=0.10; CC=0.10; LD=0.08; DF=0.07; WP=0.05; BL=0.05. Sum=1.00
Rationale: HEVC components (H+E+V+C) retain 65% of total weight — they represent the immediate physical and socio-economic risk to communities. Environmental components (CC+LD+DF+WP+BL) share 35% — they represent longer-term forcing and amplification mechanisms. This split reflects the project's primary community resilience mandate while fully integrating environmental dimensions.
Sensitivity_Model: S1: equal weights (0.111 each); S2: hazard dominant (H=0.35 CC=0.13 others proportional); S3: environment dominant (CC+LD+DF+WP+BL total 0.60)
Notes: ERI v2.0 does NOT replace G35 HEVC v1.0. G35 remains the primary risk output for reporting continuity. G64 ERI v2.0 is a parallel output showing the fuller environmental picture. Both must be published and compared — see 26_eri.py compare_with_g35() function.
